questions.question: What is the main problem that encoder-decoder models with attention solved for machine translation?
options: The inability to handle different word orders and lengths between languages.
The need for a dictionary for every word.
questions.explanation: Standard encoder-decoder models compressed everything into a single vector. Attention allows the model to 'look back' at specific parts of the source sentence, handling flexible alignments and long-range dependencies across languages.

questions.question: Why is 'sacrebleu' the recommended tool for reporting BLEU scores?
options: It normalizes tokenization so scores are comparable across different implementations.
It is faster than other BLEU implementations.
It is the only tool that can calculate chrF.
It doesn't require a reference translation.
questions.explanation: Different tokenizers produce different BLEU scores. SacreBLEU ensures that everyone uses the same tokenization scheme, making research benchmarks actually comparable.

questions.question: What is 'hallucination' in the context of machine translation?
options: When the model produces fluent-sounding text that is not supported by the source.
When the model refuses to translate a sentence.
When the model translates into the wrong target language.
When the model uses too many emojis.
questions.explanation: Hallucination occurs when a model adds facts, names, or details that weren't in the original text, often because the domain vocabulary is unfamiliar to the model.

questions.question: Which metric is considered the 2026 production default for neural evaluation of MT quality?
questions.explanation: COMET (Cross-lingual Optimized Metric for Evaluation of Translation) is a learned metric that correlates much more highly with human judgment than n-gram overlap metrics like BLEU.
